one_month_reasoning: AMD's Q3 2026 report is expected around 2026-11-03 (unconfirmed, per historical pattern), i.e. just after the 2026-10-30 window, so no company earnings fall inside it. In-window chain events: TSMC Q3 results and September/October monthly sales (mid-October), Intel Q3 results (late October), hyperscaler Q3 results with capex updates (Alphabet/Microsoft/Meta/Amazon typically last week of October), SK Hynix/Samsung Q3 (late October). These are read-through events that have mostly been positive (TSMC raised 2026 growth to >40%, Intel and Nvidia both say CPU/GPU demand exceeds supply), but the stock is up ~280% in a year and trading near its $639 high, so positioning risk is two-sided. With no company-specific scheduled catalyst, I stay close to a symmetric lognormal centred on spot (~$606 median) with monthly vol of about 72%/sqrt(12) = 21%, i.e. slightly wider than the brief's annual/3.5 rule because realized vol is elevated and the hyperscaler capex prints land inside the window.

fair_value.method: Blend of P/E on estimated NTM EPS at Sep-2027 (~$19.5 x 30x = $585) and EV/sales on CY2028 revenue (~$100B x 10x EV/S, plus ~$10B net cash, over ~1.75B diluted shares incl. partial warrant dilution = $577).

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: NTM (Q4'27-Q3'28) non-GAAP EPS ~$19.5 x 30x forward P/E; diluted shares ~1.75B (1.66B + partial vesting of OpenAI/Meta warrants)

inputs_detail.derivation: Consensus FY2027 $15.57 rising fast (33 up vs 3 down revisions); DC revenue guided to more than double in 2027 as MI450/Helios ramps for OpenAI (6GW), Meta (6GW), Anthropic (2GW, from 1H27) and Oracle; hyperscaler 2027 capex consensus >$1T (+~40%). Rolling forward one year at ~30-35% EPS growth from FY2027 gives ~$19-21; I take $19.5 net of warrant dilution.
Q2 2026 diluted count 1.659B plus roughly 90M of the up to 320M penny warrants (160M OpenAI, 160M Meta) assumed to vest by late 2027 on deployment milestones; final OpenAI tranche needs ~$600 price.

Stock currently ~39x FY2027 consensus ($604/$15.57); by Sep-2027 growth decelerates from ~80-100% DC growth toward 30-40%, so multiple compresses toward high-growth semi peers; Nvidia with 75% gross margin and ~$108B quarterly guide is the ceiling comparable. 30x is a modest premium to large-cap semi averages for >30% EPS growth.

methods.name: EV/sales
methods.inputs: CY2028 revenue ~$100B x 10x EV/sales = $1.0T EV + ~$10B net cash, / 1.75B shares

inputs_detail.derivation: 2026 ~ $50B (Q1-Q4 run-rate from $11.5B Q2, $13B Q3 guide, Q4 Helios shipments); 2027 ~ $78B with DC >2x per management; 2028 ~ +25% as OpenAI/Meta later gigawatt tranches deploy, partly offset by weak PC units (IDC: memory shortage persists through 2027).
Implies ~27x earnings at ~38% op margin; AMD gross margin 56% vs Nvidia 75% justifies a discount to Nvidia's sales multiple.

bear.story: AI capex digestion in 2027 (hyperscalers funding capex with debt per FactSet, investor skepticism already visible after Alphabet's July print), MI450/Helios ramp slips on HBM4 or rack integration, PC units fall ~10-20% on memory costs, and warrants dilute ~15-19%; EPS ~$14 at 22x.

base.story: Helios ships from late Q3 2026 and ramps through 2027 across OpenAI, Meta, Oracle and Anthropic; DC revenue roughly doubles in 2027; EPYC keeps taking server share (34.5% units, 46% vs Xeon SP); NTM EPS ~$19.5 at ~31x with partial warrant dilution.

bull.story: AI compute scarcity persists (TSMC CoWoS sold out, Nebius raising EPYC pricing, Intel/Nvidia supply-limited), AMD becomes a clear second GPU source with >$25 NTM EPS and the market keeps ~38-40x.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$360 (-40%) the stock would be pricing either a material MI450/Helios slip or cut to the OpenAI/Meta gigawatt deployments, or a broad hyperscaler capex cut for 2027 - i.e. FY2027 EPS falling back toward ~$12-13 at a low-20s multiple. With 72% realized vol a 25-30% drawdown is ordinary; a 40% one would most likely be fundamental.

reasoning: Industry lane read: the whole chain says AI compute demand still exceeds supply - Nvidia guided FQ3 to $108B (+~12% q/q) with DC up 117% y/y; TSMC raised 2026 growth to >40% with CoWoS sold out; Intel says Xeon demand outpaces supply; Nebius raised EPYC pricing; hyperscaler 2026 capex ~$725B with 2027 consensus >$1T. AMD specifically is gaining server CPU share (Mercury: 34.5% units, 46.4% vs Xeon SP) and client share (mobile ~29%), while memory shortages depress PC units (IDC -11.3% 2026) - a manageable drag since Client+Gaming is now <35% of revenue. Samsung HBM4 is the primary MI450 memory source and is sold out for 2026. Against that, at $604 AMD is ~$1T market cap, ~39x FY2027 consensus EPS of $15.57, and warrants for up to 320M shares (~19%) vest as deployments and price milestones are hit, so much of the good news is priced; consensus target is ~$617. My fair value ~$580 (P/E and EV/sales) is near spot. Scenarios 25/50/25 at $320/$610/$1000 give a mean ~$635 and a median near spot. I translate this into a lognormal with median ~$595 and sigma ~0.55 (below 72% realized, since realized vol is inflated by the rerating year, but still wide given binary AI-capex exposure), giving P(>=604) ~0.49. One-month: no AMD earnings in window; symmetric around spot.
